This project proposal looks at responsive layouts. First, a short overview of responsive layouts is given. The main question here is how responsive layouts works in practice. Responsive layouts matters because many systems depend on it.

Background
Earlier work describes two common approaches to responsive layouts. Most textbooks start from a simple model of responsive layouts. Responsive layouts has been studied for many years. The course notes explain the basic terms used for responsive layouts.

Objectives
The second objective is to build a small prototype that uses responsive layouts. The last objective is to check the prototype with a few users. The first objective is to describe how responsive layouts is used today.

Method
Each test about responsive layouts was repeated five times. The code for responsive layouts was kept in one repository. The experiment was run on a laptop with the default settings. The results were written to a csv file after every run.

Risks
The biggest risk is that responsive layouts takes longer than planned. A second risk is that the data may not be available in time.

Conclusion
The main finding is that responsive layouts improves the result. More work on responsive layouts is needed in the future. In conclusion, responsive layouts worked as expected.
